title: Meet Lognac
narration: Hi, this is team Asuzu. I built Lognac. It's an agent for reviewing medicines at hospital discharge. It compares the patient's medication history, conditions and allergies with hospital orders, discharge prescriptions and take-home instructions. Its written report links each concern to a source. An optional graph shows the connections.

title: Why it matters
narration: I built it because records can disagree as a patient goes home. A medicine may be missing, a dose may change without explanation, or instructions may conflict with an allergy. Lognac gathers the evidence and waits for a documented clinician decision.

title: Optional evidence graph
narration: The optional graph shows those same source links.

title: A missed dose change, fixed
narration: In a fictional case, home and hospital records said five milligrams of amlodipine; both discharge documents said ten. The first version missed it because those documents agreed. I fixed that comparison and added a test. Now Lognac flags the change and asks a clinician whether it was intended. It never chooses the dose.

title: Entire: change impact
narration: Entire mapped Lognac's review function: its callers, dependencies and data flows. That helped me check what a change might affect. The full test suite now passes seventeen tests.

title: cfo.ai: business plan
narration: With cfo.ai, I built three hypothetical hospital-site scenarios, a twelve-month cash view, and a review of pricing, NHS procurement and clinical governance risks. These are assumptions, not sales or validated prices.

title: Neatlogs: failure and recovery
narration: Neatlogs showed what happened inside an agent run. In a deliberate test, the medicine alert check timed out. Its trace shows the failed step, Lognac's retry and the review continuing. The trace stays red because it preserves that error. I compared it with a successful run and a later trace of the repaired dose-change workflow.

title: What is ready
narration: Lognac uses fictional UK records. It helps clinicians review discrepancies. It does not prescribe.
